base_context.deduplication: DOI, arXiv ID, canonical URL, YouTube video ID and candidate-rule intent were compared against the current shared updates. The control-voltage paper is a reading-depth upgrade of SRC-DYN-20260913-201140-05, not a newly discovered title.

novelty: Upgraded arXiv:2606.18573 from abstract-only to selected full-text methods, results, dataset and limitations.
Separates gain-reduction trajectory accuracy from waveform and short-time-energy proxy scores.
Adds a reproducible compressor test contract: quasi-static ramp, multiple-duration bursts, sub-threshold alignment probe and programme material.
Treats dry-feature centroids and dynamic histograms as diagnostic priors, not genre or section targets.
Adds song-disjoint and unseen-parameter validation requirements for learned compressor models.

source_cards.title: Evaluating Dynamic Range Compressor Models Using Control-Voltage Measurements: an Approach and Dataset
limited_findings: In the authors' ten single-example fitting experiments, direct gain-reduction loss recovered the measured control trajectory better than waveform L1 or MSTE objectives.
Waveform proxy metrics compressed the observed separation: the spread between best and worst direct gain error was 85.9%, versus 2.8% for waveform L1 and 13.3% for MSTE in that experiment.
A quasi-static level ramp exposes the response curve; bursts expose attack/release and programme dependence; a sub-threshold probe supports latency alignment.
Nominal threshold and attack labels need not equal response-defined threshold or effective attack because the hardware curve is gradual and loop gain alters ballistics.
limitations: The comparison fitted ten models to ten individual 30-second examples and evaluated each on the same example; it was not a generalization study.
Training was restricted to 10:1 ratio and fixed single-time-constant release because the tested torchcomp topology could not represent the SSL's lower-ratio curvature or auto-release behavior.
No subjective listening test establishes that lower control-trajectory error always produces the preferred musical result.
The direct control-voltage method requires access to an internal or exposed gain-control signal; ordinary plugins usually expose only meters, not ground-truth CV.

source_cards.title: Black-Box Optimization for Identifying and Inverting Audio Dynamic Range Control Effects
limited_findings: Dynamic-histogram descriptors were more useful than several conventional features for moving synthetic inversions toward the dry reference within this experiment.
Parameter error and recovered-signal feature distance disagreed: a parameter estimate closer to ground truth did not always yield the closest selected-feature reconstruction.
Non-differentiable feature objectives can be optimized without differentiable DSP, but the reported methods were far slower than real time.
limitations: Only 25 mono 30-second excerpts were used: five excerpts from each of classical, rock, electronic, pop and jazz.
Compression/expansion and inversion used one known model family and 30 synthetic profiles; transfer to unknown hardware, multiband processors or full stereo rock production is unproven.
The dry target was a single training-set centroid per effect type, which can erase genre, instrument, section and artistic-role differences.
No listening test validated naturalness or musical preference; reported CPU time was 124 to 530 seconds per 30-second excerpt.

source_cards.title: Solid State Bus-Comp: A Large-Scale and Diverse Dataset for Dynamic Range Compressor Virtual Analog Modeling
limited_findings: The dataset uses 175 unmastered songs and 220 SSL 500 G-Bus parameter combinations; paper reports 2528.53 hours.
The benchmark split separates 112 training songs from 63 test songs and reserves 76 parameter combinations as unseen controls.
Time-varying conditioning generally mattered more than simply enlarging several architectures, supporting explicit temporal validation of compressor models.
limitations: Benchmarks use waveform L1 and multi-resolution STFT losses, exactly the proxy family later shown by Thompson and Heilemann not to be equivalent to direct gain-trajectory error.
No subjective listening test is reported, and genre/instrument annotations include model-generated labels.
The paper's 2528.53-hour figure conflicts with the project page's 2258-hour overview; the paper value is retained with this discrepancy flagged.
The dataset audio license and redistribution terms were not unambiguously stated on the read paper/project page, so no Reference Card or raw-audio ingestion is authorized.
Published training used a single NVIDIA H200 for 500,000 steps; no paid computation was run for this update.

source_cards.title: AQFeatures: Objective Audio Quality Characterization — DRC Discrimination
limited_findings: The implementation expects paired original and processed files and ranks descriptors with an inverse-Fisher-style profile-variance to audio-content-variance criterion.
This supports testing whether a descriptor reacts to compression profiles while remaining less dependent on the source programme.
limitations: The repository itself warns that the research-oriented code may not exactly reproduce the cited 2017 results.
Static inspection only; MATLAB pipeline and audio were not run.
The non-commercial license prevents treating the code as an unrestricted production dependency.

knowledge_cards.title: Measure compressor behavior on the gain trajectory when it is observable
knowledge_cards.claim: Output waveform similarity is not an equivalent measure of gain-reduction behavior because phase, filtering, noise and carrier amplitude affect the proxy.
knowledge_cards.boundary: Direct GR accuracy does not establish musical preference; retain loudness-matched listening.

knowledge_cards.title: A compressor test needs static, ballistic, alignment and programme probes
knowledge_cards.claim: A slow level ramp, multiple-duration bursts, a sub-threshold alignment signal and real music expose different failure modes that one loop cannot reveal.
knowledge_cards.boundary: The paper's amplitudes and SSL switch values are reproducibility details, not recommended mix settings.

knowledge_cards.title: Nominal milliseconds are not behavioral equivalence
knowledge_cards.claim: Detector topology, gain smoothing, knee curvature, feedback loop and programme dependence can make equal attack/release labels produce different GR trajectories.
knowledge_cards.boundary: Do not infer a listening preference from the trajectory alone.

knowledge_cards.title: Dynamic histograms describe redistribution, not the correct artistic target
knowledge_cards.claim: Amplitude-distribution descriptors can detect compression effects missed by single peak/RMS values, but a global dry centroid can erase style, section and instrument role.
knowledge_cards.boundary: The study used synthetic mono inversions and no subjective listening test.

knowledge_cards.title: Parameter recovery and audible recovery are different objectives
knowledge_cards.claim: A lower parameter MSE can coexist with a worse selected-feature reconstruction, so an automatic system must state whether it is estimating controls, recreating output, or restoring a dry signal.
knowledge_cards.boundary: Neither objective substitutes for a listener-rated musical outcome.

knowledge_cards.title: Hold out both songs and control settings
knowledge_cards.claim: Compressor validation should separate unseen programme material from unseen parameter combinations; success on one axis does not prove the other.
knowledge_cards.boundary: Dataset diversity still does not prove preference on the project's rock material.

knowledge_cards.title: Temporal conditioning is a model requirement, not a proof of sound quality
knowledge_cards.claim: On the Solid State Bus-Comp benchmark, several time-varying conditioning methods generalized better than simple conditioning, but objective waveform rankings were architecture- and metric-dependent.
knowledge_cards.boundary: No listening test and no direct GR-ground-truth metric were used in that benchmark.

knowledge_cards.title: Cross-study metric disagreement is a required warning
knowledge_cards.claim: A dataset benchmark can rank models with waveform L1/M-STFT while a later direct-CV study shows those proxies may obscure GR behavior; both results can be true because they measure different targets.
knowledge_cards.boundary: This is a methodological reconciliation, not evidence that a particular model sounds better.

candidate_rules.name: validate_exposed_gain_trajectory_before_proxy_scores
candidate_rules.when: a compressor or learned model exposes an internal gain-reduction trajectory
candidate_rules.change: compare predicted GR directly with the reference trajectory and retain waveform, spectral and listening measures as separate axes
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: no mix-setting range; direct GR L1 is the paper's evaluated behavioral metric
candidate_rules.undo: reject promotion if lower GR error does not survive musical listening or causes unacceptable coloration

candidate_rules.name: require_four_part_compressor_probe
candidate_rules.when: validating threshold, ratio, knee, attack, release or latency
candidate_rules.change: run a quasi-static ramp, several burst durations, a below-threshold alignment probe and programme audio
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: paper reproduction option: 1 kHz ramp -48 to 0 dB at 1.6 dB/s and steady bursts 4 to 14 dB above threshold; these are measurement stimuli, not music settings
candidate_rules.undo: invalidate the test if level calibration, alignment or nonlinear coloration is conflated with gain modulation

candidate_rules.name: do_not_match_compressors_by_nominal_time_labels
candidate_rules.when: comparing processors or transferring a preset between compressor designs
candidate_rules.change: match the measured response and musical outcome rather than copying attack/release numbers
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: no universal range; tested SSL labels were 0.1/0.3/1/3/10/30 ms attack and 0.1/0.3/0.6/1.2 s/Auto release, retained only as hardware dataset metadata
candidate_rules.undo: cancel transfer if next-event recovery, body or transient behavior diverges despite equal labels

candidate_rules.name: hold_out_songs_and_controls_for_learned_DRC
candidate_rules.when: evaluating any learned or fitted dynamics processor
candidate_rules.change: report separate results for unseen songs and unseen control combinations, including role- and section-specific rock material
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: project proposal: at least song-disjoint and parameter-disjoint partitions; no percentage promoted from the paper
candidate_rules.undo: withhold model acceptance when either split leaks or only aggregate performance is reported

candidate_rules.name: treat_dynamic_histogram_target_as_advisory
candidate_rules.when: using amplitude distributions or dry-feature centroids to recommend compression
candidate_rules.change: condition the histogram by active events, articulation, instrument role and section; use it as evidence, not an optimization target
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: no compressor range; histogram binning and windows must be recorded per implementation
candidate_rules.undo: reject the recommendation if global matching flattens intentional contrasts or improves only the selected descriptor

candidate_rules.name: separate_behavior_color_and_preference_scores
candidate_rules.change: report gain behavior, waveform/spectral coloration and listener preference as three non-collapsed score groups
candidate_rules.parameter_range_and_origin: no setting range; separation follows the studies' metric disagreement
candidate_rules.undo: do not promote a single composite score if weighting changes the winner

experiments.title: Compressor behavior contract on one plugin
experiments.success: nominal parameter changes produce distinct, explainable trajectories and preferred variants survive matched listening
experiments.cancel: hidden makeup, misalignment or unavailable gain trace prevents behavioral interpretation

experiments.title: Direct gain trajectory versus waveform proxy ranking
experiments.material: free subset of the SSL bus compressor control-voltage dataset; files not downloaded in this run
experiments.success: metric disagreement is quantified and not hidden in one aggregate score
experiments.cancel: license, dataset size or hardware/CV safety prevents a controlled local subset

experiments.title: Global versus event-and-section dynamic histograms
experiments.success: conditioned views explain audible differences that the global distribution hides
experiments.cancel: event detector errors merge articulations or section labels are unreliable

experiments.title: Multiband isolation baseline for rock drum bus and mix bus
experiments.success: any benefit remains after crossover-only and full-band baselines
experiments.cancel: multiband wins only by loudness, static tonal shift or hidden crossover coloration

conflicts.issue: Solid State Bus-Comp ranks models with waveform L1 and M-STFT; the later direct-CV study shows waveform proxies need not preserve ranking of gain-trajectory error.
conflicts.resolution: Store behavior, coloration and listening outcomes separately; do not declare either metric universally correct.

conflicts.issue: Dataset duration is 2528.53 hours in the paper but 2258 hours on the project page.
conflicts.resolution: Retain the paper figure for paper-specific claims and flag the project-page inconsistency.

tool_status.arxiv_mcp: not_verified_connected; public primary arXiv HTML used

handoff: Validate compressor behavior with ramp, bursts, alignment probe and programme audio. When a true GR trajectory exists, compare it directly; keep waveform/spectral color and listener preference separate. Do not transfer attack/release labels between processors as equivalent behavior. Condition dynamic histograms by event, articulation and section; retain no-DRC and level-only baselines.
